I added `GET /api/admin/users/recently-created`. It returns the logins of users created in the last 7 days, newest first. It is restricted to admins. I haven't built or run anything, as you asked, so none of it is compiled or tested.

- **Repository:** `UserRepository.findLoginsByCreatedDateGreaterThanEqual(Instant since)` is a JPQL query that selects only the logins.
- **Service:** `UserService.getRecentlyCreatedUserLogins()` computes the cutoff as `Instant.now(clock).minus(7, DAYS)`, following `docs/conventions.md`. This meant adding a `Clock` constructor parameter to `UserService`. I found no existing `new UserService(` calls in `src`, so nothing else should need updating.
- **Resource:** `UserResource.getRecentlyCreatedUsers()` uses `@PreAuthorize` with `AuthoritiesConstants.ADMIN`, as the other admin endpoints do.
- **Clock bean:** The project had no `Clock` bean, so I added `config/ClockConfiguration.java`, which provides `Clock.systemUTC()`.

The new `/users/recently-created` path doesn't clash with `/users/{login}`, because Spring prefers the literal path.

I didn't add tests. I also skipped the `notes/` updates from your vault rules, since the project has no `notes/index.md`.
